title: Geopolitical Daily
email_subject: Democrats take Congress; what changes now
preheader: They also flipped Texas, Kansas and Georgia, and Trump announced an Israel aid cutoff.
intro_text: Good morning. It's Wednesday, November 04, 2026 — the 3 stories that matter most today, plus 2 updates on stories you're following and 2 quick items from around the world.

stories.story_title: Democrats win the House and Senate in a sweeping midterm rebuke
stories.why_important: Democrats won control of both the House and Senate on Tuesday, projections show. The win ends Republican rule of Congress and lets Democrats block Trump's agenda. It also lets them investigate his administration during his final two years. Voters pointed to living costs, tariffs, fuel prices and the war with Iran.
stories.what_overlooked: A Senate majority also lets Democrats confirm or reject judges. They can run hearings on the Iran war, powers that outlast the wave itself.
stories.prediction: Trump's first public response to the results is expected within 72 hours. It will show whether he fights the new Congress or bargains with it.

stories.story_title: Trump says US military aid to Israel will end this year
stories.why_important: On Fox News, Trump said he and Netanyahu agreed to stop aid to Israel. The aid is about $4 billion a year and would stop after 2026. The US would still sell Israel weapons, but Trump gave no details. Israeli officials have not publicly confirmed any deal.
stories.what_overlooked: Haaretz says the earlier-than-planned cutoff actually fits Netanyahu's goal of a 'Super Sparta' Israel. That Israel would build its own weapons with US partnership.
stories.prediction: A public statement from Netanyahu's office within 72 hours will settle the question. It will show whether the deal is real or an election-day remark.

stories.story_title: Bomb threats target five European flights; no explosives found
stories.why_important: Reuters and DW reported that five airliners received bomb threats the same day. The five threatened airliners were flying to Warsaw, Rome, Sofia and Spain. Every plane landed safely and searches found nothing, but the timing forced disruptions across several European airports.
stories.what_overlooked: No group has claimed the threats, and no arrests were reported. So it remains unknown whether this was one campaign or a copycat hoax wave.
stories.prediction: Polish and Italian police will say within days whether one source sent the threats. Any arrests would point to an organized campaign.

quick_hits.text: Students blockaded dozens of French high schools and universities, demanding more funding, better facilities and more university places.
The International Monetary Fund cleared the release of a $294 million bailout tranche to Jordan.

big_number.context: CGTN reports the IMF expects sub-Saharan Africa's economy to grow 4.5% in 2026 and 2027, even as debt costs rise.

views.framing: Democrats’ midterm win is a sweeping rebuke to Trump, driven by economic anger and his handling of war.
views.quote: Election Day turned into a massive rebuke of President Donald Trump

perspective_grid.blindspot: Indonesian police arrested three people for allegedly tapping President Prabowo Subianto’s phone; reports suggest a suspect may be a senior official. The case matters abroad because it raises surveillance and governance concerns at the top of a Southeast Asian state.

developing.text: Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms won Georgia's governor race, becoming the first Black woman elected governor of any US state.
First lady Melania Trump will host Russian and Ukrainian delegations at the White House to discuss the Oleshky ceasefire and humanitarian mission.
